title: Universal-counit normalization of the ringed scalar/pullback shift square
statement:
Let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_Y)$ be a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R_Y\to S_Y$ and $R_X\to S_X$ be maps of commutative ring sheaves, with structure maps $g^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ and $g^{-1}S_Y\to S_X$ making the coefficient square commute. Work in the unbounded module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ for scalar change, $L_g^R,L_g^S$ for the two ringed derived pullbacks. Use their fixed cochain shifts and their universal derived counits/units, computed from flat-term K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. The scalar shifts are normalized by the scalar universal derived counits [lem-pur-coefficient-scalar-shifts].

Let $\theta_g:L_g^S C_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}C_XL_g^R$ be the canonical balanced derived comparison: on resolving complexes it is the comparison between the two iterated sheaf tensor products induced by the commuting ring square, and its derived normalization is by these universal counits. Then $\theta_g$ commutes with the fixed integer shifts. Explicitly, for $H_1=L_g^SC_Y,H_2=C_XL_g^R$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$,
$$\sigma_{H_2,K,n}\,\theta_{g,K[n]}=(\theta_{g,K})[n]\,\sigma_{H_1,K,n},$$
using the composite shift convention of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. No boundedness, coefficient flatness, properness or constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Apply cochainUniversalCounitTransport to the universal homotopy-category pair of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback. Its first clause gives universality of the prescribed derivedCochainCounit; its second clause transfers invertibility on every flat-term independently K-flat complex. Uniqueness of left derived pairs identifies this cochain pair with the supplied pair. Cancel the invertible comparison component to prove pull_counit_isIso for the supplied counit. This reuses the existing transport theorem and contains no separate proof of Kan precomposition or change along an isomorphism.

Lift the existing scalarAssociation termwise and use mapHomologicalComplexCompIso on its source and target. This gives a natural transformation beta whose component is exactly kappa. The standard termwise lift, composition comparisons, and their inverses commute with every integer shift. The supplied NatTrans.CommShift hypotheses on the four counits imply the same for their whiskered composites b1 and b2, and localization of beta.

Resolve a representative of K by a flat-term independently K-flat P using lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Convert the resolution flatness convention to IsFlatOnSite using siteSheafTensorRightIso from lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits. Quasi-isomorphism inversion and essential surjectivity give Q(P) isomorphic to K. Ringed pullback preserves flat terms and K-flatness. Apply step 1 to eR at P and eX at pull(f)(P), using extensionPullback for scalar extension. Hence b2 at P is invertible; b1 need not be shown invertible.

Shifts preserve independent K-flatness: for any acyclic A, tensor(A,P[n]) is isomorphic to tensor(A,P)[n] by the total-tensor integer-shift isomorphism. The latter is acyclic by shift closure of the homotopy acyclic subcategory. Flatness of terms of P[n] is flatness of P in degree i+n. Thus the normalization hypothesis applies to both P and P[n].

The private shift_on_model lemma writes the shift equation for b1 followed by localized beta. Substitute normalization at P and P[n], then the shift equation for b2 and naturality of theta along the shift comparison of Q. Cancel the shifted invertible component b2(P) and the image of the shift comparison of Q. This proves the required equation at Q(P). Both sides are components of natural transformations from shift followed by CY followed by LS to LR followed by CX followed by shift. Naturality transports their equality along Q(P) isomorphic to K, proving the stated equation for arbitrary K and n.

The delivery adds a proof only: no new nodes, statement and stmt_deps unchanged. The proof follows the 0D6D pattern (flat-term K-flat representative, two iterated termwise pullbacks). Step 1: preserves-kflat allows u=id and a nonflat c, so both intermediate complexes are flat-term K-flat and the counits b_1, b_2 are invertible. Step 2: checked the balanced map and its inverse; A_0-balancing holds exactly by the commuting square v(a)=w(a), and both composites are the identity by B- and D-balancing. Step 3: F_i is additive, so the shifted differential is (-1)^n F_i(d) and t_i is the identity with no sign; P[n] stays K-flat via s^2_n. Step 4: both counits are shift-compatible (scalar by lem-pur-coefficient-scalar-shifts, pullback by the right-Kan lemma with Q and termwise pullback shift-compatible), then whiskered and composed. Step 5: the three-line cancellation and the transport to arbitrary K via h are correct. Advisory points, none of them a fault: (1) commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker is stated for [1]; extending to all integer n is a routine coherence induction. (2) 'Fixed cochain shifts' of L_g must be read as the counit-normalized (resolution-shift) structure; step 4 makes this explicit, it matches the sibling lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit, and a (-1)^n twist of one pullback's shifts would break the equation. Edge cases checked: n=0, n=±1, identity maps, zero ring, nonflat Z->Z/2. No duplicate found in the DAG (scalar-only, exact-inverse-image and tensor shift nodes are different statements). Off-unit kflat-resolution and kflat-complex are Lean-closed; the declared tool_uses are accepted. No SGA cited.
